source_policy: Runtime party-ordering rules distilled into cses_wiki. Country folders and processed examples are development references only.

lower_house_vote_share.description: Use the relevant lower-house election result as the main party-ordering source.
lower_house_vote_share.ordering_basis: Parties are ordered by lower-house vote share for the election covered by the study. In two-vote systems, use the party-list or national party vote rather than the district-candidate vote.

upper_house_vote_share_when_applicable.description: Use upper-house results only for upper-house variables or when the upper-house election is the CSES main election.
upper_house_vote_share_when_applicable.ordering_basis: Upper-house vote share may drive upper-house party variables, but it should not replace the main lower-house party order unless explicitly approved for the study.

presidential_first_round_vote_share.description: For presidential election studies, presidential first-round results define the main presidential candidate or party order unless CSES project guidance requires another basis.
presidential_first_round_vote_share.ordering_basis: Use first-round presidential vote share as the default presidential ordering basis. Second-round participation is documented separately.

presidential_second_round_context_only.description: Second-round presidential results are needed for second-round vote variables, but are not enough by themselves to define the full party order.
presidential_second_round_context_only.ordering_basis: Use second-round results only with the approved first-round or main-election party order and document non-contesting parties as not applicable where required.

processor_review_required.description: Election context or electoral system is not clear enough to compute party order automatically.
processor_review_required.ordering_basis: Processor and macro coder must identify the correct election result table and ordering rule before party coding proceeds.

validation_rules: Party A-I order must match the selected ordering basis or have a recorded approved override.
Party A-I labels must be consistent across micro vote-choice variables, party batteries, leader batteries, macro party variables, labels, and documentation.
Others or aggregate residual rows must not be assigned a Party A-I slot unless explicitly approved under CSES rules.
Numeric party codes must be unique and must match the approved party table.
Micro processor and macro coder approval are required before final party recoding, labels, macro party variables, or party appendix documentation are marked ready.
